selected_evidence.text_span: Om (also written as Aum) is the sacred primordial sound and symbol of the universe in Hindu philosophy. According to the Mandukya Upanishad, Om encompasses all of existence: the past, present, and future. It is considered the sound of Brahman, the ultimate reality, and is used as a mantra in meditation and spiritual practice.

Prana is the vital life force or breath that sustains all living beings. According to the Upanishads, prana is the fundamental energy that animates the body and mind. The Prashna Upanishad teaches that prana is the supreme force from which all life originates, and it pervades the entire universe as the vital breath.

The Upanishads expound the secret meaning of the Vedas and treat of Brahma, according to [2]. They are considered the crowning part of the Veda, providing knowledge about the ultimate reality and the self. [1] also mentions the importance of being properly instructed by knowers of the Brahman, implying that the Upanishads contain teachings on spiritual growth and self-realization.

The Bhagavad Gita emphasizes the importance of doing one's duty (dharma) and performing actions (karma yoga) without attachment to their outcomes [1]. It states that action is higher than inactivity and that one must always do their duty, as inaction will not even allow one to sustain their body. The Gita also advises individuals to act dispassionately and offer their actions as a sacrifice, which will help them attain freedom from the cycle of rebirth. Additionally, it highlights the interdependence of individuals and the divine, suggesting that by performing their duties and offering their actions as a sacrifice, they will receive the support and nourishment they need [1].

According to the Narada-Purana [1], the opposite of Ahimsa (Non-Violence) is not explicitly mentioned. However, it can be inferred that the opposite of Ahimsa is Adharma (unrighteousness) or Himsa (violence), which is mentioned in the context of Ahimsa being the bestower of Yogic achievements.
